user_query: What makes LINE-SGD faster than graph factorization when it is trained with ordinary SGD on the language network?
llm_response: LINE-SGD is faster because, on the language network, it uses a much simpler objective and update rule than graph factorization: it optimizes only local pairwise edge information with negative sampling, avoids expensive matrix-factorization-style computations over the whole graph, and can be trained efficiently with ordinary SGD using sparse, edge-based updates. This makes each iteration cheaper and the optimization more scalable on large networks.
llm_confidence_reasoning: This is a well-established explanation of why LINE-style methods are faster, but the exact wording depends on the specific paper and implementation details, so I am not fully certain every phrasing matches the source.
